title: Spring Boot Web Applications
description: Production Spring Boot reference covering starters, dependency injection, configuration, profiles, validation, MVC, WebFlux boundaries, errors, data access, transactions, security, resilience, testing, Actuator, observability, AOT, containers, and deployment.

subtopics.title: Starters, Auto-Configuration & Application Startup
subtopics.description: Starters align dependency sets; auto-configuration contributes beans when classes, properties, and missing-bean conditions match. Keep the application class near the root package.

callouts.title: Read the Condition Evaluation Report
callouts.text: When an expected bean is missing or surprising configuration appears, inspect auto-configuration conditions before adding manual configuration or component scanning.

subtopics.title: Beans, Dependency Injection & Configuration Classes
subtopics.description: Prefer constructor injection, immutable dependencies, explicit module configuration, and narrow bean APIs. Avoid service locators and hidden field injection.

callouts.title: Avoid Circular Dependencies
callouts.text: A cycle usually signals mixed responsibilities or incorrect module direction. Redesign ownership or introduce an event/domain boundary rather than enabling circular references.

subtopics.title: Configuration Properties, Profiles & Secrets
subtopics.description: Bind related settings into validated typed properties, use profiles for coherent environment modes, and inject secrets through a managed secret source rather than source control.

codeBlocks.code:
payments:
  base-url: ${PAYMENTS_BASE_URL}
  timeout: 3s
management:
  endpoints.web.exposure.include: health,info,prometheus

callouts.title: Profile Explosion Hides Behavior
callouts.text: Prefer one shared configuration model with external values. Do not encode every customer, region, and feature combination as overlapping profiles.

subtopics.title: Spring MVC Controllers & Validation
subtopics.description: Use request DTOs at the HTTP boundary, Bean Validation for structural constraints, service methods for use cases, and response DTOs that expose only public fields.

callouts.title: Validation Does Not Authorize
callouts.text: A valid ID or DTO does not prove the caller owns the resource or may perform the action. Enforce current policy in the service/domain boundary.

subtopics.title: Exceptions, Problem Details & Request Boundaries
subtopics.description: Translate expected domain failures into stable HTTP Problem Details and correlation IDs; treat unexpected exceptions as server faults without exposing internals.

callouts.title: Do Not Catch Everything in Controllers
callouts.text: Centralize transport mapping while preserving domain context and causal chains internally. Redact SQL, stack traces, paths, tokens, and personal data from responses.

subtopics.title: Spring Data, Transactions & Connection Pools
subtopics.description: Define repository methods from aggregate access patterns, keep transactions short around authoritative state changes, and size pools from database capacity rather than request concurrency.

callouts.title: Proxy-Based Transactions Need Visible Boundaries
callouts.text: Self-invocation, private methods, async work, checked-exception policy, and calls made before proxy interception can surprise transactional behavior. Test rollback and propagation explicitly.

subtopics.title: Spring Security, Sessions & Authorization
subtopics.description: Build an explicit SecurityFilterChain, choose session or bearer-token architecture deliberately, protect CSRF where browser credentials are ambient, and enforce method/domain authorization.

callouts.title: URL Rules Are Only One Layer
callouts.text: Also authorize object ownership, tenant, state transition, and field visibility. Validate JWT issuer/audience/algorithm and keep administrative Actuator endpoints isolated.

subtopics.title: MVC vs WebFlux & Blocking Boundaries
subtopics.description: Spring MVC uses a thread-per-request model with blocking libraries; WebFlux uses non-blocking event loops and reactive streams. Choose one from the dependency stack and workload, not fashion.

rows: Too many blocked threads or unbounded work

callouts.title: Reactive Does Not Make Blocking Dependencies Non-Blocking
callouts.text: JPA, many SDKs, filesystem calls, and legacy clients still block. Isolate them deliberately or use a compatible stack; never block an event loop casually.

subtopics.title: Timeouts, Retries, Caching & Messaging
subtopics.description: Set deadlines at every remote boundary, retry only transient idempotent operations with jitter and budgets, bound bulkheads, and make message consumers idempotent.

codeBlocks.code:
HTTP client: connect timeout + response deadline + cancellation
Retry: classified transient errors, capped attempts, exponential backoff + jitter
Cache: authoritative source, TTL, invalidation, stampede control
Messaging: transaction/outbox, idempotency key, poison handling, DLQ policy

callouts.title: Do Not Stack Independent Retries
callouts.text: Client, load balancer, service, database, and queue retries multiply load during failure. Assign retry ownership and propagate deadlines and attempt context.

subtopics.title: Unit, Slice & Integration Testing
subtopics.description: Use plain unit tests for domain logic, focused Spring test slices for one framework layer, and full integration tests with real infrastructure contracts where behavior matters.

callouts.title: Do Not Load the Whole Context by Default
callouts.text: Full context tests are valuable for wiring and end-to-end behavior but slower and less diagnostic. Match test scope to the contract under test and use production-like databases for SQL semantics.

subtopics.title: Actuator, Health, Metrics & Tracing
subtopics.description: Actuator exposes operational endpoints; distinguish liveness from readiness, secure exposure, publish application metrics, and integrate logs/traces through Micrometer and OpenTelemetry-compatible pipelines.

codeBlocks.code:
management:
  endpoint.health.probes.enabled: true
  endpoints.web.exposure.include: health,info,prometheus
  tracing.sampling.probability: 0.1
  observations.key-values:
    service: orders

callouts.title: Health Checks Must Be Cheap and Purposeful
callouts.text: Liveness should not fail because a dependency is temporarily unavailable. Readiness may reflect inability to serve, but aggressive dependency checks can amplify outages.

subtopics.title: AOT, Containers & Production Checklist
subtopics.description: Build reproducibly, choose JVM or native deployment from measured needs, use layered images/buildpacks, run as non-root, configure memory ergonomics, and drain gracefully.

callouts.title: Native Images Change Runtime Assumptions
callouts.text: AOT/native builds need reflection, resources, proxies, serialization, agents, startup, memory, and observability verified from the emitted artifact. Benchmark representative steady-state and cold-start workloads.

callouts.title: Production Checklist
callouts.text: Pin Java/Boot dependencies, validate typed config, use constructor injection, authorize every action, bound pools/timeouts/retries, test transactions and migrations, secure Actuator, export telemetry, scan images, run least-privileged, and rehearse shutdown and rollback.
